# upload/cursors — the Vercel deploy folder

Generated by `npm run build` (from the repo root) and committed, so the hosted
site always matches the repo — same pattern as THIN ICE's `upload/zinc`.
**Do not edit these files by hand; the next build overwrites them.**

There is no build step for Vercel to run. It serves this folder as-is.

## One-time Vercel setup

1. vercel.com → Add New → Project → import the CURSORS repo.
2. **Root Directory**: `upload/cursors`
3. **Framework Preset**: Other. Leave Build Command and Output Directory **empty**.
4. Deploy. Every `git push` after that updates the site automatically.

## What is in here

| | |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | the page — tiny, loads the rest |
| `assets/` | one JS bundle + one CSS file, with ~130 XP icons and the 80 MSN emoticons inlined into them (small files cost more as requests than as bytes) |
| `media/` | the four CC-BY MP3s and the XP sound scheme, **fetched only when something plays them** |
| `vercel.json` | cache headers — filenames are content-hashed, so assets are immutable for a year and only `index.html` revalidates |

First paint is about **0.5 MB gzipped**. The 8 MB of audio never touches a
visitor who does not open Winamp, and a redeploy only re-downloads the HTML and
the code bundle — every unchanged asset stays in the browser cache.

## The game server is separate

This folder is only the client. It talks to the beta server at
`wss://cursors.34-70-75-204.sslip.io` (see `server/DEPLOY.md`). If that server is
down the site still works — it falls back to the offline single-player sandbox.
Add `?server=off` to the URL to force the sandbox, or `?server=wss://...` to
point at a different server.
